implemented: production desktop surfaces keep a long-lived adjacent shell-provider-host process so generation-bound menu tokens remain valid through invocation
provider traffic uses framed typed requests over redirected pipes and validates request identity before accepting a response
menu enumeration is bounded to 200 milliseconds and falls back to a functional local menu without blocking desktop input
menu invocation is bounded to 2 seconds and a failed or mismatched host is terminated before a later request can restart it
real desktop items expose Open, Rename, Delete, and Properties through both pointer right-click and Shift+F10
desktop background exposes Refresh, Sort by name, and New folder through both pointer right-click and Shift+F10
pointer, keyboard, and accessibility menu activation all produce the same generation- and selection-bound MenuInvocation
Properties delegates to the Windows properties verb while mutation commands return to the existing admitted desktop-operation routes
New folder is confined to the resolved user Desktop root, validates the requested name, and resolves collisions without overwrite
Escape, arrow navigation, submenu traversal, disabled state, and accessible menu/menuitem roles are represented by the shared MenuModel
deliberately_not_claimed: third-party native shell-extension enrichment; the isolated host currently publishes the deterministic built-in command set and reports optional_enrichment_complete=false
pixel-identical placement and styling relative to the Windows 10 native context menu
commands: cargo check -p desktop-ui -p platform-win -p shell-provider-host -p superdesktop-app --offline
cargo clippy -p desktop-ui -p platform-win -p shell-provider-host -p superdesktop-app --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings
cargo test -p desktop-ui -p platform-win -p shell-provider-host -p superdesktop-app --offline
